aliases: Ta Xue Lan Fei orchid scented green tea
processing: Sold as an orchid-scented green tea. One retailer describes tender Mengding Xue Ya buds scented with spring orchids from Huangshan and Sichuan; no independent record of the method was found.
harvest_season: Not documented for this tea. Mengding greens are usually spring teas, with early pickings the most prized.
appearance_dry: No standard description is recorded; expect a small, tender green leaf, as is typical of fine Mengding greens.
appearance_liquor: Typically pale yellow-green and clear, as with fine Mengding greens.
appearance_wet: Typically small, tender green shoots, as with fine Mengding greens.
taste_profile: Sold as orchid-scented, so expect a floral aroma over a soft, sweet green tea. No detailed tasting record for this name exists.

brewing.notes: General advice for scented greens: keep water cool and early steeps short, as the scent comes out first.

vintage_note: Little is documented about how it is sold. Like scented greens in general, it is best bought from the most recent harvest and drunk within about a year, before the aroma fades.
description:
Meng Ding Lan Fei is an orchid-scented green tea sold under the name of Mengding Mountain in Ya'an, one of Sichuan's historic tea places. It is a rare name, appearing mainly in a few specialist retail lists, and what is known comes from those sellers.

One retailer, using the name Ta Xue Lan Fei, describes tender Xue Ya buds scented with spring orchids. Beware the name: Ta Xue Lan Fei is also used for a different orchid-scented yellow tea from Huo Shan in Anhui.

Expect flowers first and a gentle green tea underneath, and brew it as you would any delicate scented green, cool and short. A real floral note should fade gently over steeps; a loud, unchanging perfume is a reason to doubt a tea of this type.

Ask the seller who makes it and whether real orchid was used. A similar tea, Meng Ding Snow Orchid, was described by an English-language tea writer in 2010 as a new scented style built on a Ganlu-type base. Whether the two are related is not established.
history: Little is documented about this tea: its maker and date of origin are unclear. It should not be read as one of Mengding's old tribute teas. A similar orchid-scented Mengding green, Snow Orchid, was described in 2010 as newly reaching the market in small quantities, which suggests the style may be recent.
